extracted.intended_audience: institutional signing officials, account administrators, principal investigators, applicants, reviewers, and other eRA Commons users (research administrators for organizations registering with or using eRA Commons)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step procedural guidance for registering an organization in eRA Commons, creating SO/AA and user accounts, and the multiple supported login methods (eRA credentials, Login.gov, InCommon federated, PIV/CAC) including associating two-factor authentication and troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format and maximum size
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments should be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award and closeout actions available in Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: Use eRA Commons to view the notice of award (NoA) and other key documents; submit Just-in-Time (JIT) information required prior to final award decision; submit required documentation including the Financial Status Report/Federal Financial Report and Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) to close out a grant; submit a No-Cost Extension notification; submit an annual progress report electronically; manage personal and institutional profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must use two-factor authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal investigators, reviewers, and key personnel associated with an application or an RPPR are required to use two-factor authentication for enhanced security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-factor authentication can be through a federated (organization) account if it meets NIH required security requirements, or through the use of Login.gov. If required to transition, the user will receive a message guiding them through using Login.gov with eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available login methods
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four login methods to access eRA Commons: Login.gov, eRA credentials (username/password), InCommon federated account (organization credentials), and PIV/CAC smartcard (for internal NIH/federal staff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA credentials are being phased out; external users will be required to associate a two-factor authentication account (Login.gov or Federated) to authenticate and then access their eRA account. The modules accessible to a user depend on their role and privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login.gov one-time association requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To use Login.gov you must create a Login.gov account and associate it, one-time only, with your existing eRA Commons account by entering your current eRA username and password on the Associate your eRA Account screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use the new Login.gov credentials for association—use the eRA Commons credentials you had prior to setting up Login.gov. After association, you must use Login.gov to log in. You will retain and must maintain your eRA username and password separately (change eRA password once per year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Login.gov account setup requirements and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a Login.gov account, provide an email you will always have access to, create a strong password following guidelines, and choose an authentication method (phone, code list, authenticator app, security key, or government employee ID).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose phone authentication, use a cell phone (not VOIP). After adding a phone, you'll receive an SMS code to verify. Tip: select 'Remember this browser' to reduce repeated two-factor prompts on the same machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: InCommon federated account requirements and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: To use an InCommon Federated account, your organization must participate in the InCommon federation and support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards; your account must have two-factor set up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the organization does not support NIH two-factor standards or you have not set up two-factor, you will not be able to log in via InCommon and will be required to use Login.gov. Errors during the flow may come from NIH or from the organization's sign-in site. Contact your Organization Administrators for organization-specific issues; eRA Service Desk cannot help with the organization's login screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO) requirement for organization registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization must be registered in eRA Commons by a person who has signature authority to legally bind the organization in grants administration matters (Signing Official, SO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of NIH-accepted signing officials include: Corporation - President or CEO; Institute - Executive Director; University - President, Dean, or Chancellor. During registration, accounts for the SO and an Account Administrator (AA) are created. The first SO can create additional SO accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications due on or after January 25, 2022, applicants must have a UEI at the time of application submission. If you choose NIH Grants or Non‑NIH Grants during registration you must provide a UEI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a UEI you must have previously registered in SAM.gov. NOTE: If your organization intends to only apply for Other Transaction Authority (OTA) opportunities, then a UEI is not required for initial registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing recommendations for organization registration
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH recommends starting the organization registration process six weeks prior to your deadline to allow time to address unforeseen issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA Commons registration can take up to 10 business days to complete, so plan in advance. The assignment of a UEI is sufficient to register in eRA Commons while full SAM.gov registration is processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration wizard steps and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration process consists of a five-step wizard: Step 1 Purpose (select registration intent and opportunity types); Step 2 Verify Identification (enter/verify UEI or indicate you don't have one); Step 3 Institution Details (many fields auto-populated from SAM.gov; specify Closeout and NoA emails); Step 4 Accounts (create SO and optionally AA; read username criteria); Step 5 Review & Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Next button becomes enabled only when required options are completed. If SAM.gov provides data for fields, those fields are not editable in eRA; correct them in SAM.gov if wrong. If Institution State is disabled, first specify Institution Country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email verification and account activation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting a registration request you will receive an email to verify your email address; you must click the link within eight days or your registration request will be canceled. After approval you will receive emails confirming registration, account creation (username), and temporary password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary password is valid only for 48 hours. You must log into eRA Commons within two days of receiving the temporary password or request a password reset. After changing the temporary password you are required to log back in and the SO will be presented with and must acknowledge the Acknowledgment of Signing Official Responsibilities form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Username permanence and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Usernames are permanent once submitted and cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the displayed username criteria during account creation; the username and password identify you throughout the Commons system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account lockout and session expiration policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons locks users out after three unsuccessful login attempts. Work sessions expire after 45 minutes of inactivity and the system returns to the Commons Login screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If locked out, use Forgot Password/Unlock Account link to reset password or contact SO/AO to reactivate account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated organization selection after login
rubrics_metrics.description: After logging in, confirm that the correct organization is displayed if you are affiliated with multiple institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The displayed organization affects the information and modules you can access in Commons. See Changing to a Different Affiliated Organization for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting Login.gov/InCommon problems before contacting support
rubrics_metrics.description: Before contacting the eRA Service Desk if Login.gov or Federated login does not work, perform basic troubleshooting steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear browser cache/history and restart the browser; ensure you are not using an old bookmarked URL (use https://public.era.nih.gov/commonsplus/); if still not working, contact the eRA Service Desk at https://www.era.nih.gov/need-help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association process prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Before associating your eRA account with Login.gov or an InCommon Federated account, ensure your eRA Commons account is active and you know your eRA password, and that you are not using old bookmarked URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure of your eRA password, use the Forgot Password/Unlock Account link and follow the reset process (submit User ID and email, get temporary password via email, change password). Only then return to the Associate your eRA Account screen to enter the correct eRA credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: InCommon special notes for administrative accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: InCommon Federated accounts, previously limited to only eRA scientific accounts, are opened up to eRA administrative accounts effective September 15, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have more than one eRA administrative account, wait to switch any of your administrative accounts as eRA is working on a solution that will support users with multiple eRA accounts.
